class ErrorCollector:
    """Accumulates every failure. Validators never short-circuit, so the client
    fixes everything in one round trip instead of playing whack-a-mole.

    Messages never echo attacker-controlled input back (that is how reflected
    XSS and log injection creep in) and never disclose account existence.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_errors", "_seen")

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._errors: list[FieldError] = []
        self._seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()

    def add(self, field_: str, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        key = (field_, code)
        if key in self._seen:
            return
        self._seen.add(key)
        self._errors.append(FieldError(field_, code, message))

    def has(self, field_: str) -> bool:
        return any(e.field == field_ for e in self._errors)

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return not self._errors

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self._errors)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._errors)

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[FieldError]:
        return iter(self._errors)

    def to_list(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        order = {"email": 0, "username": 1, "password": 2, "display_name": 3}
        return [
            e.to_dict()
            for e in sorted(self._errors, key=lambda e: (order.get(e.field, 99), e.code))
        ]

def script_of(ch: str) -> str:
    cp = ord(ch)
    if ch.isascii() and not ch.isalpha():
        return "Common"
    for lo, hi, name in _SCRIPT_RANGES:
        if lo <= cp <= hi:
            return name
    if unicodedata.combining(ch):
        return "Inherited"
    return "Common"


def scripts_in(s: str) -> set[str]:
    found = {script_of(c) for c in s}
    return found - {"Common", "Inherited"}


def is_mixed_script(s: str) -> bool:
    found = scripts_in(s)
    if len(found) <= 1:
        return False
    return not any(found <= combo for combo in _SAFE_SCRIPT_COMBOS)


def skeleton(s: str) -> str:
    """UTS #39-style skeleton: everything that *looks* alike maps to one string.

    Stored alongside the username with a UNIQUE index, so "pаypal" (Cyrillic а)
    cannot be registered once "paypal" exists.
    """

    s = "".join(_CONFUSABLE_MAP.get(c, c) for c in s)
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", s)
    return "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.combining(c))

def deleet(s: str) -> str:
    """Fold leetspeak so 'a$$h0le' matches the profanity list."""
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", s).casefold()
    s = "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    s = s.translate(_LEET)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z]+", "", s)


def scan_codepoints(value: str, field_: str, errs: ErrorCollector) -> None:
    """Reject dangerous codepoint classes on any user-supplied string."""
    if "\x00" in value:
        errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_NULL_BYTE, "Value must not contain null bytes.")
    for ch in value:
        cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
        if ch in BIDI_CONTROL:
            errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_BIDI_CONTROL,
                     "Value must not contain bidirectional control characters.")
        elif ch in INVISIBLE:
            errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_INVISIBLE_CHARS,
                     "Value must not contain zero-width or invisible characters.")
        elif cat == "Cc" and ch not in "\t":
            errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_CONTROL_CHARS,
                     "Value must not contain control characters.")
        elif cat == "Co":
            errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_PRIVATE_USE,
                     "Value must not contain private-use characters.")
        elif cat == "Cs":
            errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_LONE_SURROGATE,
                     "Value contains an invalid surrogate character.")
        elif cat == "Cn":
            errs.add(field_, Code.FIELD_UNASSIGNED,
                     "Value contains an unassigned Unicode character.")


def clean_whitespace(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalise exotic spaces to U+0020, collapse runs, trim edges."""
    for sp in UNICODE_SPACES:
        s = s.replace(sp, " ")
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    original: str      # exactly what the user typed (trimmed) — for display
    normalized: str    # local@punycode-lowercased-domain — what we mail
    canonical: str     # provider aliases folded — uniqueness key only
    local: str

    unicode_domain: str


def _canonicalize_provider(local: str, domain: str) -> str:
    """Fold provider-specific aliases so one mailbox = one account.

    Trade-off: this blocks the legitimate "one +tag per service" workflow. It is
    behind CANON_ALIASES because for some products that workflow matters more
    than alias-based multi-accounting.
    """
    d = domain
    l = local
    if d in ("googlemail.com", "gmail.com"):
        d = "gmail.com"
        l = l.split("+", 1)[0].replace(".", "")
    elif d in ("outlook.com", "hotmail.com", "live.com", "msn.com"):
        l = l.split("+", 1)[0]
    elif d in ("yahoo.com", "ymail.com"):
        l = l.split("-", 1)[0]
    elif d in ("protonmail.com", "proton.me", "pm.me", "icloud.com", "me.com", "fastmail.com"):
        l = l.split("+", 1)[0]
    else:
        l = l.split("+", 1)[0]
    return f"{l}@{d}"


def validate_email(raw: Any, errs: ErrorCollector) -> Optional[EmailResult]:
    f = "email"
    if raw is None:
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_REQUIRED, "Email is required.")
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_WRONG_TYPE, "Email must be a string.")
        return None

    scan_codepoints(raw, f, errs)
    value = clean_whitespace(raw)
    if not value:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_EMPTY, "Email is required.")
        return None
    if len(value) > settings.email_max:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_TOO_LONG,
                 f"Email must be at most {settings.email_max} characters.")
        return None

    # "Name <a@b.com>" is a header form, not an address. Accepting it invites
    # header-injection downstream in the mailer.
    if "<" in value or ">" in value or "," in value or ";" in value:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DISPLAY_FORM,
                 "Enter only the email address, without a display name.")
        return None
    if value.startswith('"'):
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_QUOTED_LOCAL,
                 "Quoted local parts are not supported.")
        return None
    if "@" not in value:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_NO_AT, "Email must contain '@'.")
        return None

    local, _, domain = value.rpartition("@")

    # --- local part ---
    if not local:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_LOCAL_EMPTY, "The part before '@' is required.")
    else:
        if len(local.encode()) > settings.email_local_max:
            errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_LOCAL_TOO_LONG,
                     f"The part before '@' must be at most {settings.email_local_max} bytes.")
        if local.startswith(".") or local.endswith(".") or ".." in local:
            errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_LOCAL_DOTS,
                     "The part before '@' has misplaced dots.")
        for atom in local.split("."):
            if atom and not _LOCAL_ATOM_RE.match(atom):
                errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_LOCAL_INVALID,
                         "The part before '@' contains unsupported characters.")
                break
        if settings.block_plus_addressing and "+" in local:
            errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_PLUS_ADDRESSING,
                     "Plus-addressed emails are not accepted.")

    # --- domain ---
    if not domain:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_EMPTY, "The part after '@' is required.")
        return None
    if domain.startswith("[") or domain.endswith("]"):
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_IP_LITERAL, "IP-literal domains are not accepted.")
        return None
    try:
        ipaddress.ip_address(domain)
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_IP_LITERAL, "IP-address domains are not accepted.")
        return None
    except ValueError:
        pass

    unicode_domain = domain.rstrip(".").lower()
    if is_mixed_script(unicode_domain):
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_CONFUSABLE,
                 "The email domain mixes character sets and cannot be accepted.")

    # IDN → punycode with UTS-46 + STD3 rules; this rejects most homograph domains.
    if _idna is not None:
        try:
            ascii_domain = _idna.encode(unicode_domain, uts46=True, std3_rules=True).decode()
        except Exception:
            errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_IDNA, "The email domain is not valid.")
            return None
    else:
        try:
            ascii_domain = unicode_domain.encode("idna").decode()
        except Exception:
            errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_IDNA, "The email domain is not valid.")
            return None
    ascii_domain = ascii_domain.lower()

    if len(ascii_domain) > settings.email_domain_max:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_TOO_LONG, "The email domain is too long.")
    labels = ascii_domain.split(".")
    if len(labels) < 2:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_NO_TLD, "The email domain must include a top-level domain.")
    for label in labels:
        if not label or len(label) > 63 or not _DOMAIN_LABEL_RE.match(label):
            errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_LABEL_INVALID, "The email domain is not valid.")
            break
    tld = labels[-1] if labels else ""
    if tld.isdigit():
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_NUMERIC_TLD, "The email domain is not valid.")
    if ascii_domain in RESERVED_DOMAINS or tld in RESERVED_TLDS:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_RESERVED,
                 "This email domain cannot receive mail and is not accepted.")

    if settings.allowed_email_domains and ascii_domain not in settings.allowed_email_domains:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED,
                 "Registration is limited to approved email domains.")
    if settings.block_disposable and (
        ascii_domain in DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS
        or any(ascii_domain.endswith(s) for s in DISPOSABLE_SUFFIXES)
    ):
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DISPOSABLE, "Disposable email addresses are not accepted.")
    if settings.block_role_accounts and local.split("+")[0].lower() in ROLE_LOCALS:
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_ROLE_ACCOUNT,
                 "Shared or role-based addresses are not accepted; use a personal address.")
    if settings.verify_mx and not _domain_has_mx(ascii_domain):
        errs.add(f, Code.EMAIL_DOMAIN_NO_MX, "The email domain cannot receive mail.")

    if errs.has(f):
        return None

    # Local part is case-sensitive per RFC; in practice every major provider
    # lowercases. We lowercase for the canonical key, preserve case for delivery.
    normalized = f"{local}@{ascii_domain}"
    canonical = (
        _canonicalize_provider(local.lower(), ascii_domain)
        if settings.canonicalize_aliases
        else normalized.lower()
    )
    return EmailResult(value, normalized, canonical, local, ascii_domain, unicode_domain)


def _domain_has_mx(domain: str) -> bool:
    try:
        import dns.resolver
        resolver = dns.resolver.Resolver()
        resolver.lifetime = 2.0
        try:
            if resolver.resolve(domain, "MX"):
                return True
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:  # implicit MX: an A record is a valid mail destination
            return bool(resolver.resolve(domain, "A"))
        except Exception:
            return False
    except ImportError:
        return True  # fail open if dnspython is absent

_USERNAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9._-]+$")
_UUID_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{8}-?[0-9a-f]{4}-?[0-9a-f]{4}-?[0-9a-f]{4}-?[0-9a-f]{12}$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UsernameResult:
    display: str     # as typed (trimmed) — shown back to the user
    normalized: str  # NFKC + casefold — UNIQUE index
    skeleton: str    # confusable-folded — second UNIQUE index


def _contains_profanity(folded: str) -> bool:
    if any(safe in folded for safe in PROFANITY_SAFE):
        # Only skip the terms actually covered by the safe word.
        remaining = folded
        for safe in PROFANITY_SAFE:
            remaining = remaining.replace(safe, "")
        folded = remaining
    return any(word in folded for word in PROFANITY)


def validate_username(raw: Any, errs: ErrorCollector) -> Optional[UsernameResult]:
    f = "username"
    if raw is None:
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_REQUIRED, "Username is required.")
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_WRONG_TYPE, "Username must be a string.")
        return None

    scan_codepoints(raw, f, errs)
    value = clean_whitespace(raw)
    if not value:
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_EMPTY, "Username is required.")
        return None

    # PRECIS UsernameCaseMapped (RFC 8265): NFKC then casefold.
    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).casefold()

    if len(normalized) < settings.username_min:
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_TOO_SHORT,
                 f"Username must be at least {settings.username_min} characters.")
    if len(normalized) > settings.username_max:
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_TOO_LONG,
                 f"Username must be at most {settings.username_max} characters.")

    # ASCII-only usernames. Restrictive on purpose: usernames appear in URLs,
    # @-mentions and audit logs, where a homograph is a real impersonation risk.
    if not _USERNAME_RE.match(normalized):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_INVALID_CHARS,
                 "Username may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens.")
    if is_mixed_script(value):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_MIXED_SCRIPT,
                 "Username must not mix characters from different alphabets.")
    if normalized and (normalized[0] in "._-" or normalized[-1] in "._-"):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_EDGE_SEPARATOR,
                 "Username must not start or end with a dot, underscore or hyphen.")
    if re.search(r"[._-]{2,}", normalized):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_REPEATED_SEPARATOR,
                 "Username must not contain consecutive dots, underscores or hyphens.")
    if normalized.isdigit():
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_ALL_DIGITS,
                 "Username must not consist only of digits.")
    if "@" in value or _LOCAL_ATOM_RE.match("") is None and "@" in normalized:
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_LOOKS_LIKE_EMAIL,
                 "Username must not be an email address.")
    if _UUID_RE.match(normalized):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_INVALID_CHARS,
                 "Username must not look like a system identifier.")

    skel = skeleton(value)
    # Reserved check runs on the skeleton, so "admın"/"аdmin" are caught too.
    stripped = skel.replace(".", "").replace("_", "").replace("-", "")
    if (
        normalized in RESERVED_USERNAMES
        or skel in RESERVED_USERNAMES
        or stripped in RESERVED_USERNAMES
        or any(normalized.startswith(p) for p in RESERVED_PREFIXES)
    ):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_RESERVED, "This username is not available.")
    if _contains_profanity(deleet(value)):
        errs.add(f, Code.USERNAME_OFFENSIVE, "This username is not available.")

    if errs.has(f):
        return None
    return UsernameResult(value, normalized, skel)


_EMOJI_RE = re.compile(
    "[" "\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF" "\U00002600-\U000027BF" "\U0001F1E6-\U0001F1FF" "]"
)
_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(https?://|www\.|\w+\.(com|net|org|io|ru|cn|xyz)\b)", re.I)


def validate_display_name(raw: Any, errs: ErrorCollector) -> Optional[str]:
    f = "display_name"
    if raw is None:
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_REQUIRED, "Display name is required.")
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_WRONG_TYPE, "Display name must be a string.")
        return None

    scan_codepoints(raw, f, errs)
    # NFC (not NFKC) preserves legitimate typography in real names.
    value = clean_whitespace(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw))
    if not value:
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_EMPTY, "Display name is required.")
        return None
    if len(value) > settings.display_max:
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_TOO_LONG,
                 f"Display name must be at most {settings.display_max} characters.")

    # Markup characters are rejected at the boundary as defence in depth. The
    # actual XSS control is contextual escaping at render time (§13) — storing
    # HTML-escaped text is an anti-pattern that corrupts data on every re-encode.
    if re.search(r"[<>&\"'`\\]", value):
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_MARKUP,
                 "Display name must not contain < > & \" ' ` or backslash.")
    if any(unicodedata.category(c) in ("Cc", "Cf") for c in value):
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_INVALID_CHARS, "Display name contains invalid characters.")

    # Zalgo: stacked combining marks break layout in every consumer of this field.
    run = 0
    for ch in value:
        run = run + 1 if unicodedata.combining(ch) else 0
        if run > 3:
            errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_ZALGO, "Display name contains too many combining marks.")
            break
    if len(_EMOJI_RE.findall(value)) > settings.display_max_emoji:
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_TOO_MANY_EMOJI,
                 f"Display name may contain at most {settings.display_max_emoji} emoji.")
    if _URL_RE.search(value):
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_URL, "Display name must not contain a web address.")

    folded = deleet(value)
    if any(term in folded for term in IMPERSONATION_TERMS):
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_IMPERSONATION,
                 "Display name must not imply an official or staff role.")
    if _contains_profanity(folded):
        errs.add(f, Code.DISPLAY_OFFENSIVE, "Display name contains disallowed language.")

    return None if errs.has(f) else value

def _levenshtein(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    if a == b:
        return 0
    if not a:
        return len(b)
    if not b:
        return len(a)
    prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j - 1] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]


def _similar(password: str, other: str, threshold: float = 0.5) -> bool:
    """True if `other` is embedded in, or close to, the password."""
    if not other or len(other) < 3:
        return False
    p, o = password.casefold(), other.casefold()
    if o in p or p in o:
        return True
    distance = _levenshtein(p, o)
    return distance / max(len(p), len(o)) < threshold


def _longest_run(s: str) -> int:
    best = run = 1
    for i in range(1, len(s)):
        run = run + 1 if s[i] == s[i - 1] else 1
        best = max(best, run)
    return best if s else 0


def _has_sequence(s: str, length: int = 4) -> bool:
    """Detect ascending/descending runs like 'abcd', '4321'."""
    low = s.casefold()
    for i in range(len(low) - length + 1):
        window = low[i:i + length]
        deltas = {ord(window[j + 1]) - ord(window[j]) for j in range(length - 1)}
        if deltas in ({1}, {-1}):
            return True
    return False


def _has_keyboard_walk(s: str, length: int = 4) -> bool:
    low = s.casefold()
    for row in KEYBOARD_ROWS:
        for i in range(len(row) - length + 1):
            chunk = row[i:i + length]
            if chunk in low or chunk[::-1] in low:
                return True
    return False


def _estimate_log10_guesses(pw: str) -> float:
    """Cheap entropy estimate. Replace with zxcvbn in production — this is a
    conservative floor, not a real password-strength model."""
    charset = 0
    if re.search(r"[a-z]", pw): charset += 26
    if re.search(r"[A-Z]", pw): charset += 26
    if re.search(r"[0-9]", pw): charset += 10
    if re.search(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", pw): charset += 33
    if any(ord(c) > 127 for c in pw): charset += 100
    charset = max(charset, 2)

    # Effective length: collapse repeated runs and monotonic sequences, since
    # neither adds search space proportional to its length.
    effective, i = 0, 0
    while i < len(pw):
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(pw) and pw[j] == pw[i]:
            j += 1
        if j - i > 1:
            effective += 1 + (j - i - 1) * 0.15
            i = j
            continue
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(pw) and ord(pw[j]) - ord(pw[j - 1]) in (1, -1):
            j += 1
        if j - i >= 3:
            effective += 1 + (j - i - 1) * 0.2
            i = j
            continue
        effective += 1
        i += 1

    import math
    guesses = effective * math.log10(charset)
    folded = deleet(pw)
    if pw.casefold() in COMMON_PASSWORDS or folded in COMMON_PASSWORDS:
        guesses = min(guesses, 3.0)
    elif any(c in folded for c in COMMON_PASSWORDS if len(c) >= 6):
        guesses -= 3.0
    # A trailing year/number is the most predictable mutation there is.
    if re.search(r"(19|20)\d{2}[!.]?$", pw):
        guesses -= 1.5
    if re.match(r"^[A-Z][a-z]+\d{1,4}[!@#]?$", pw):
        guesses -= 2.0
    return max(guesses, 0.0)

    errs: ErrorCollector,
    *,
    email: Optional[EmailResult],
    username: Optional[UsernameResult],
    display_name: Optional[str],
) -> Optional[str]:
    f = "password"
    if raw is None:
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_REQUIRED, "Password is required.")
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_WRONG_TYPE, "Password must be a string.")
        return None

    # Byte cap FIRST: this is the DoS gate. A multi-megabyte string must never
    # reach NFC normalization, entropy scoring, or the KDF.
    raw_bytes = len(raw.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass"))
    if raw_bytes > settings.password_max_bytes:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_TOO_MANY_BYTES,
                 f"Password must be at most {settings.password_max_bytes} bytes.")
        return None
    if len(raw) > settings.password_max:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG,
                 f"Password must be at most {settings.password_max} characters.")
        return None
    if "\x00" in raw:
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_NULL_BYTE, "Password must not contain null bytes.")
        return None
    if any(unicodedata.category(c) == "Cc" for c in raw):
        errs.add(f, Code.FIELD_CONTROL_CHARS, "Password must not contain control characters.")

    # RFC 8265 OpaqueString: NFC only. NFKC would collapse distinct passwords
    # and silently destroy entropy.
    pw = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw)

    if not pw:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_EMPTY, "Password is required.")
        return None
    if not pw.strip():
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_ALL_WHITESPACE, "Password must not be only whitespace.")
        return None
    # Reject rather than silently trim: trimming mutates the user's secret.
    if pw != pw.strip():
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_EDGE_WHITESPACE,
                 "Password must not start or end with whitespace.")
    if len(pw) < settings.password_min:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT,
                 f"Password must be at least {settings.password_min} characters.")

    if _longest_run(pw) > settings.password_max_repeat:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_REPEATED,
                 f"Password must not repeat a character more than {settings.password_max_repeat} times.")
    if _has_sequence(pw):
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_SEQUENTIAL,
                 "Password must not contain long sequential runs such as 'abcd' or '1234'.")
    if _has_keyboard_walk(pw):
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_KEYBOARD_WALK,
                 "Password must not contain keyboard patterns such as 'qwerty'.")
    if pw.casefold() in COMMON_PASSWORDS or deleet(pw) in COMMON_PASSWORDS:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_COMMON, "This password is too common. Choose another.")
    if settings.service_name and settings.service_name.casefold() in pw.casefold():
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_SERVICE_NAME,
                 "Password must not contain the name of this service.")

    if username and _similar(pw, username.normalized):
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_SIMILAR_USERNAME,
                 "Password must not be similar to your username.")
    if email:
        if _similar(pw, email.local) or _similar(pw, email.canonical.split("@")[0]):
            errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_SIMILAR_EMAIL,
                     "Password must not be similar to your email address.")
    if display_name:
        if _similar(pw, display_name) or any(
            _similar(pw, part) for part in display_name.split() if len(part) >= 4
        ):
            errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_SIMILAR_DISPLAY,
                     "Password must not be similar to your display name.")

    # Composition rules are deliberately NOT enforced (NIST SP 800-63B advises
    # against them); we gate on estimated strength instead, so a long passphrase
    # passes and "P@ssw0rd!" does not.
    if _estimate_log10_guesses(pw) < settings.password_min_log10_guesses:
        errs.add(f, Code.PASSWORD_TOO_SIMPLE,
                 "Password is too easy to guess. Use a longer or more varied password.")

    return None if errs.has(f) else pw

_argon2_hasher = (
    PasswordHasher(
        time_cost=settings.argon2_time,
        memory_cost=settings.argon2_memory_kib,
        parallelism=settings.argon2_parallelism,
        hash_len=32,
        salt_len=16,
        type=Argon2Type.ID,

    else None

def _pepper(password: str) -> bytes:
    """HMAC the password with a server-held key before the KDF.

    A database-only leak (SQLi, backup theft) then yields hashes that cannot be
    cracked offline without also compromising the application secret. As a bonus
    for bcrypt this produces a fixed 32-byte input, sidestepping both the 72-byte
    truncation and the NUL-byte truncation bug.
    """
    return hmac.new(settings.pepper, password.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).digest()


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    """Return a self-describing record: scheme$pepper_version$hash."""
    peppered = _pepper(password)
    scheme = settings.hash_scheme
    if scheme.startswith("argon2") and _ARGON2:
        digest = _argon2_hasher.hash(peppered)
        return f"argon2id${settings.pepper_version}${digest}"
    if _BCRYPT:
        # base64 so the value is ASCII and NUL-free before bcrypt sees it.
        material = base64.b64encode(peppered)
        digest = _bcrypt.hashpw(material, _bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=settings.bcrypt_rounds))
        return f"bcrypt${settings.pepper_version}${digest.decode()}"
    digest = _argon2_hasher.hash(peppered)
    return f"argon2id${settings.pepper_version}${digest}"


def verify_password(password: str, record: str) -> bool:
    """Constant-time-ish verification. Included for completeness — login uses it."""
    try:
        scheme, _version, digest = record.split("$", 2)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    peppered = _pepper(password)
    if scheme == "argon2id" and _ARGON2:
        try:
            return _argon2_hasher.verify(digest, peppered)
        except argon2_exceptions.VerificationError:
            return False
        except Exception:
            return False
    if scheme == "bcrypt" and _BCRYPT:
        return _bcrypt.checkpw(base64.b64encode(peppered), digest.encode())
    return False


_DUMMY_HASH_INPUT = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)


def burn_hash_cycles() -> None:
    """Perform equivalent KDF work on paths where we skip real hashing, so the
    duplicate-email path costs the same wall-clock as the create path."""
    try:
        hash_password(_DUMMY_HASH_INPUT)
    except Exception:
        pass


def blind_index(value: str) -> str:
    """Deterministic keyed hash used as the uniqueness index for emails.

    Storing HMAC(key, canonical_email) instead of a plaintext unique index means
    a leaked index alone does not disclose the membership list, while still
    enforcing one-account-per-address at the database level.
    """
    return hmac.new(settings.blind_index_key, value.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

try:
    import httpx
    _HTTPX = True
except ImportError:
    _HTTPX = False

_breach_cache: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
_breach_cache_lock = threading.Lock()


async def is_password_breached(password: str) -> tuple[bool, int]:
    """Check Have I Been Pwned without ever transmitting the password.

    Only the first 5 hex chars of the SHA-1 leave this process; HIBP returns
    every suffix in that bucket and we match locally. SHA-1 here is a lookup
    key defined by the API, never a storage mechanism.
    """
    if not settings.check_breached or not _HTTPX:
        return False, 0

    sha1 = hashlib.sha1(password.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest().upper()
    prefix, suffix = sha1[:5], sha1[5:]

    with _breach_cache_lock:
        cached = _breach_cache.get(prefix)
    if cached is not None:
        return suffix in cached, 0

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=settings.breach_timeout) as client:
            resp = await client.get(
                f"https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/{prefix}",
                headers={"Add-Padding": "true", "User-Agent": f"{settings.service_name}-registration"},
            )
            resp.raise_for_status()
        suffixes: dict[str, int] = {}
        for line in resp.text.splitlines():
            part, _, count = line.partition(":")
            try:
                n = int(count)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if n > 0:  # padding entries report 0
                suffixes[part.strip().upper()] = n
        with _breach_cache_lock:
            if len(_breach_cache) > 2048:
                _breach_cache.clear()
            _breach_cache[prefix] = set(suffixes)
        return suffix in suffixes, suffixes.get(suffix, 0)
    except Exception as exc:
        # Fail open: a provider outage must not halt all registrations. The
        # local COMMON_PASSWORDS list still applies as a floor.
        log.warning("Breach check unavailable: %s", type(exc).__name__)
        if settings.breach_fail_open:
            return False, 0
        raise

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RateLimitRule:
    name: str
    limit: int
    window_seconds: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RateLimitDecision:
    allowed: bool
    retry_after: int = 0
    rule: str = ""


class SlidingWindowLimiter:
    """In-process sliding-window log.

    Correct for a single instance. For a fleet, back it with the Redis Lua
    script below so the limit is global rather than per-pod.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._hits: dict[str, deque[float]] = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._last_gc = time.monotonic()

    def _gc(self, now: float) -> None:
        if now - self._last_gc < 60:
            return
        self._last_gc = now
        for key in [k for k, v in self._hits.items() if not v or now - v[-1] > 86400]:
            self._hits.pop(key, None)

    def check(self, key: str, rule: RateLimitRule, *, record: bool = True) -> RateLimitDecision:
        now = time.monotonic()
        bucket_key = f"{rule.name}:{key}"
        with self._lock:
            self._gc(now)
            bucket = self._hits.setdefault(bucket_key, deque())
            cutoff = now - rule.window_seconds
            while bucket and bucket[0] < cutoff:
                bucket.popleft()
            if len(bucket) >= rule.limit:
                retry = int(bucket[0] + rule.window_seconds - now) + 1
                return RateLimitDecision(False, max(retry, 1), rule.name)
            if record:
                bucket.append(now)
        return RateLimitDecision(True)


limiter = SlidingWindowLimiter()

# Redis-backed equivalent (atomic; use when running more than one instance):
REDIS_SLIDING_WINDOW_LUA = """
local key, now, window, limit = KEYS[1], tonumber(ARGV[1]), tonumber(ARGV[2]), tonumber(ARGV[3])
redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, 0, now - window)
local count = redis.call('ZCARD', key)
if count >= limit then
  local oldest = redis.call('ZRANGE', key, 0, 0, 'WITHSCORES')
  return {0, math.ceil(oldest[2] + window - now)}
end
redis.call('ZADD', key, now, ARGV[4])
redis.call('EXPIRE', key, window)
return {1, 0}
"""


def client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    """Resolve the real client IP without trusting spoofable headers.

    X-Forwarded-For is attacker-controlled unless every hop is ours. We take the
    address exactly `trusted_proxy_hops` from the right; with 0 configured we
    use the socket peer and ignore the header entirely.
    """
    peer = request.client.host if request.client else "0.0.0.0"
    hops = settings.trusted_proxy_hops
    if hops <= 0:
        return peer
    xff = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for", "")
    if not xff:
        return peer
    parts = [p.strip() for p in xff.split(",") if p.strip()]
    if len(parts) < hops:
        return peer
    candidate = parts[-hops]
    try:
        return str(ipaddress.ip_address(candidate))
    except ValueError:
        return peer


def subnet_of(ip: str) -> str:
    """Group by /24 (v4) or /48 (v6): a single actor rarely owns just one IP."""
    try:
        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
    except ValueError:
        return ip
    if addr.version == 4:
        return str(ipaddress.ip_network(f"{ip}/24", strict=False))
    return str(ipaddress.ip_network(f"{ip}/48", strict=False))


def enforce_rate_limits(ip: str, email_domain: str = "", email_key: str = "") -> RateLimitDecision:
    if not settings.rate_limit_enabled:
        return RateLimitDecision(True)
    checks: list[tuple[str, RateLimitRule]] = [
        ("global", RateLimitRule("global", settings.rl_global_min, 60)),
        (ip, RateLimitRule("ip_hour", settings.rl_ip_hour, 3600)),
        (ip, RateLimitRule("ip_day", settings.rl_ip_day, 86400)),
        (subnet_of(ip), RateLimitRule("subnet_hour", settings.rl_subnet_hour, 3600)),
    ]
    if email_domain:
        checks.append((email_domain, RateLimitRule("domain_hour", settings.rl_domain_hour, 3600)))
    if email_key:
        # Keyed on the blind index, never on the raw address.
        checks.append((email_key, RateLimitRule("email_day", settings.rl_email_day, 86400)))
    for key, rule in checks:
        decision = limiter.check(key, rule)
        if not decision.allowed:
            return decision
    return RateLimitDecision(True)

def issue_csrf_token() -> str:
    """Signed, timestamped double-submit token: nonce.timestamp.hmac"""
    nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    ts = str(int(time.time()))
    payload = f"{nonce}.{ts}"
    sig = hmac.new(settings.csrf_secret, payload.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    return f"{payload}.{base64.urlsafe_b64encode(sig).decode().rstrip('=')}"


def validate_csrf(header_token: str, cookie_token: str) -> bool:
    if not header_token or not cookie_token:
        return False
    # Timing-safe: a byte-by-byte comparison leaks the token prefix.
    if not hmac.compare_digest(header_token, cookie_token):
        return False
    try:
        nonce, ts, sig_b64 = header_token.rsplit(".", 2)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    payload = f"{nonce}.{ts}"
    expected = hmac.new(settings.csrf_secret, payload.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    expected_b64 = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(expected).decode().rstrip("=")
    if not hmac.compare_digest(sig_b64, expected_b64):
        return False
    try:
        age = time.time() - int(ts)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return 0 <= age <= settings.csrf_ttl


def origin_allowed(request: Request) -> bool:
    origin = request.headers.get("origin")
    if origin:
        return origin.lower().rstrip("/") in settings.allowed_origins
    referer = request.headers.get("referer")
    if referer:
        from urllib.parse import urlparse
        parsed = urlparse(referer)
        return f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.netloc}".lower() in settings.allowed_origins
    # No Origin and no Referer: not a browser form post. Token check still applies.
    return True

SCHEMA = """
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id                  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    email               TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_canonical     TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_blind_index   TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_verified      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

    username_normalized TEXT NOT NULL,
    username_skeleton   TEXT NOT NULL,
    display_name        TEXT NOT NULL,

    status              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending_verification',
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

-- The database is the arbiter of uniqueness, not an application-level SELECT.
-- Two concurrent signups both pass a pre-check; only the constraint is atomic.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_users_email_bi   ON users(email_blind_index);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_users_username   ON users(username_normalized);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_users_skeleton   ON users(username_skeleton);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_verification_tokens (
    token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- store the hash, never the token
    user_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    used_at    TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS registration_audit (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    at          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    ip_hash     TEXT NOT NULL,            -- hashed: audit logs are PII too
    outcome     TEXT NOT NULL,
    reason      TEXT,
    request_id  TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CreateOutcome:
    created: bool
    user_id: Optional[str]
    conflict: Optional[str]  # 'email' | 'username' | 'skeleton' | None


class Database:
    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self._path = path
        self._local = threading.local()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.executescript(SCHEMA)

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = getattr(self._local, "conn", None)
        if conn is None:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(self._path, timeout=10, isolation_level=None)
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
            self._local.conn = conn
        return conn

    def username_exists(self, normalized: str, skel: str) -> bool:
        conn = self._connect()
        # Parameterized. String interpolation here would be the SQLi hole.
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE username_normalized = ? OR username_skeleton = ? LIMIT 1",
            (normalized, skel),
        ).fetchone()
        return row is not None

    def create_user(
        self,
        *,
        email: str,
        email_canonical: str,
        email_bi: str,
        username: str,
        username_normalized: str,
        username_skeleton: str,
        display_name: str,
        password_hash: str,
    ) -> CreateOutcome:
        conn = self._connect()
        user_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        try:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            conn.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO users (
                    id, email, email_canonical, email_blind_index,
                    username, username_normalized, username_skeleton,
                    display_name, password_hash, password_updated_at, status
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'), 'pending_verification')
                """,
                (
                    user_id, email, email_canonical, email_bi,
                    username, username_normalized, username_skeleton,
                    display_name, password_hash,
                ),
            )
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
            return CreateOutcome(True, user_id, None)
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            detail = str(exc)
            if "email_blind_index" in detail:
                return CreateOutcome(False, None, "email")
            if "username_skeleton" in detail:
                return CreateOutcome(False, None, "skeleton")
            if "username_normalized" in detail:
                return CreateOutcome(False, None, "username")
            return CreateOutcome(False, None, "unknown")

    def store_verification_token(self, user_id: str, token: str, ttl_seconds: int = 86400) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        token_hash = hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest()
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO email_verification_tokens (token_hash, user_id, expires_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, datetime('now', ?))",
            (token_hash, user_id, f"+{int(ttl_seconds)} seconds"),
        )

    def audit(self, ip: str, outcome: str, reason: str, request_id: str) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        ip_hash = hmac.new(settings.blind_index_key, ip.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:32]
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO registration_audit (ip_hash, outcome, reason, request_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (ip_hash, outcome, reason, request_id),
        )

        return any(issue.field == field for issue in self.issues)

    def details(self) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
        order = {
            "body": 0,
            "email": 1,
            "username": 2,
            "password": 3,
            "display_name": 4,
        }
        indexed = list(enumerate(self.issues))
        indexed.sort(key=lambda pair: (order.get(pair[1].field, 99), pair[0]))

        return [
            {
                "field": issue.field,
                "code": issue.code,
                "message": issue.message,
            }
            for _, issue in indexed
        ]


class APIProblem(Exception):
    def __init__(
        self,
        status: int,
        code: str,
        message: str,
        *,
        details: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None,
        headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.details = details
        self.headers = headers or {}


class DependencyUnavailable(Exception):
    pass


def problem_response(
    status: int,
    code: str,
    message: str,
    *,
    details: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> JSONResponse:
    error: dict[str, Any] = {
        "code": code,
        "message": message,
    }
    if details is not None:
        error["details"] = details

    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=status,
        content={"error": error},
        headers=headers,
    )

def connect_database() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    connection = sqlite3.connect(
        str(DATABASE_PATH),
        timeout=5.0,
        isolation_level=None,
    )
    connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    connection.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
    connection.execute("PRAGMA trusted_schema = OFF")
    return connection


def initialize_database() -> None:
    DATABASE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if DATABASE_PATH.exists() and DATABASE_PATH.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("DATABASE_PATH must not be a symbolic link")

    connection = connect_database()
    try:
        connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        connection.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL")
        connection.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                id                  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                email               TEXT NOT NULL,
                email_lookup        BLOB NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                username            TEXT NOT NULL,
                username_key        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                username_skeleton   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                password_hash       TEXT NOT NULL
                    CHECK (password_hash LIKE '$argon2id$%'),
                display_name        TEXT NOT NULL,
                status              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'disabled')),
                created_at          INTEGER NOT NULL
            );

            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rate_limit_events (
                bucket              BLOB NOT NULL,
                created_at          INTEGER NOT NULL
            );

            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_rate_limit_bucket_time
                ON rate_limit_events(bucket, created_at);
            """
        )
    finally:
        connection.close()

    DATABASE_PATH.chmod(0o600)


def keyed_digest(purpose: str, value: str) -> bytes:
    # SHA-256 is used only inside an HMAC for lookup/rate-limit identifiers.
    # Password verifiers are exclusively Argon2id.
    material = purpose.encode("ascii") + b"\0" + value.encode("utf-8")
    return hmac.new(APP_SECRET, material, hashlib.sha256).digest()


def consume_rate_limit(
    scope: str,
    identifier: str,
    maximum: int,
    window_seconds: int,
) -> tuple[bool, int]:
    now = int(time.time())
    cutoff = now - window_seconds
    bucket = keyed_digest(f"rate-limit:{scope}", identifier)

    connection = connect_database()
    try:
        connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")

        connection.execute(
            """
            DELETE FROM rate_limit_events
            WHERE bucket = ? AND created_at <= ?
            """,
            (bucket, cutoff),
        )

        row = connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT COUNT(*) AS event_count, MIN(created_at) AS oldest
            FROM rate_limit_events
            WHERE bucket = ? AND created_at > ?
            """,
            (bucket, cutoff),
        ).fetchone()

        count = int(row["event_count"])
        if count >= maximum:
            oldest = int(row["oldest"] or now)
            retry_after = max(1, oldest + window_seconds - now)
            connection.execute("COMMIT")
            return False, retry_after

        connection.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO rate_limit_events(bucket, created_at)
            VALUES (?, ?)
            """,
            (bucket, now),
        )

        # Probabilistic cleanup prevents unbounded growth without performing a
        # full-table deletion on every request.
        if secrets.randbelow(128) == 0:
            connection.execute(
                """
                DELETE FROM rate_limit_events
                WHERE created_at <= ?
                """,
                (now - 172_800,),
            )

        connection.execute("COMMIT")
        return True, 0
    except Exception:
        if connection.in_transaction:
            connection.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        connection.close()


def insert_user(
    *,
    email: str,
    email_lookup: bytes,
    username: str,
    username_key: str,
    username_skeleton: str,
    password_hash: str,
    display_name: str,
) -> bool:
    """Returns True when inserted and False for any known uniqueness conflict."""

    connection = connect_database()
    try:
        connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            connection.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO users(
                    id,
                    email,
                    email_lookup,
                    username,
                    username_key,
                    username_skeleton,
                    password_hash,
                    display_name,
                    status,
                    created_at
                )
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                """,
                (
                    uuid.uuid4().hex,
                    email,
                    email_lookup,
                    username,
                    username_key,
                    username_skeleton,
                    password_hash,
                    display_name,
                    "active",
                    int(time.time()),
                ),
            )
            connection.execute("COMMIT")
            return True
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
            if connection.in_transaction:
                connection.rollback()

            # Do not depend on database-specific exception text. Verify that
            # the integrity error was one of the expected uniqueness races.
            conflict = connection.execute(
                """
                SELECT 1
                FROM users
                WHERE email_lookup = ?
                   OR username_key = ?
                   OR username_skeleton = ?
                LIMIT 1
                """,
                (email_lookup, username_key, username_skeleton),
            ).fetchone()

            if conflict is not None:
                return False
            raise
    except Exception:
        if connection.in_transaction:
            connection.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        connection.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unicode and normalization helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def has_forbidden_unicode(value: str) -> bool:
    combining_run = 0

    for character in value:
        codepoint = ord(character)
        category = unicodedata.category(character)

        if category in {"Cc", "Cf", "Cs", "Co", "Cn"}:
            return True

        # Unicode noncharacters.
        if 0xFDD0 <= codepoint <= 0xFDEF:
            return True
        if codepoint & 0xFFFF in {0xFFFE, 0xFFFF}:
            return True

        if unicodedata.combining(character):
            combining_run += 1
            if combining_run > 4:
                return True
        else:
            combining_run = 0

    return False


def utf8_size(value: str) -> int | None:
    try:
        return len(value.encode("utf-8", errors="strict"))
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        return None


def required_string(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    field_name: str,
    collector: ValidationCollector,
) -> str | None:
    if field_name not in payload:
        collector.add(
            field_name,
            "required",
            f"{field_name} is required.",
        )
        return None

    value = payload[field_name]
    if type(value) is not str:
        collector.add(
            field_name,
            "invalid_type",
            f"{field_name} must be a JSON string.",
        )
        return None

    return value


def script_name(character: str) -> str | None:
    if not character.isalpha():
        return None

    name = unicodedata.name(character, "")

    if "LATIN" in name:
        return "latin"
    if "CYRILLIC" in name:
        return "cyrillic"
    if "GREEK" in name:
        return "greek"
    if "ARABIC" in name:
        return "arabic"
    if "HEBREW" in name:
        return "hebrew"
    if (
        "CJK" in name
        or "HIRAGANA" in name
        or "KATAKANA" in name
        or "IDEOGRAPH" in name
    ):
        return "japanese"
    if "HANGUL" in name:
        return "korean"

    return name.split(" ", 1)[0].casefold() if name else None


def label_has_mixed_scripts(label: str) -> bool:
    scripts = {
        script
        for character in label
        if (script := script_name(character)) is not None
    }
    return len(scripts) > 1


def bounded_edit_distance(left: str, right: str) -> int:
    if abs(len(left) - len(right)) > 1:
        return 2

    previous = list(range(len(right) + 1))
    for left_index, left_character in enumerate(left, start=1):
        current = [left_index]
        for right_index, right_character in enumerate(right, start=1):
            current.append(
                min(
                    current[-1] + 1,
                    previous[right_index] + 1,
                    previous[right_index - 1]
                    + (left_character != right_character),
                )
            )
        previous = current

    return previous[-1]


VISUAL_TRANSLATION = str.maketrans(
    {
        "0": "o",
        "1": "l",
        "3": "e",
        "4": "a",
        "5": "s",
        "7": "t",
        "8": "b",
        "9": "g",
        "@": "a",
        "$": "s",
    }
)


def identifier_skeleton(value: str) -> str:
    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).casefold()
    translated = normalized.translate(VISUAL_TRANSLATION)
    return "".join(character for character in translated if character.isalnum())

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NormalizedEmail:
    canonical: str
    local: str
    domain: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NormalizedUsername:
    display: str
    key: str
    skeleton: str


def domain_matches(domain: str, blocked_domains: set[str] | frozenset[str]) -> bool:
    return any(
        domain == blocked or domain.endswith("." + blocked)
        for blocked in blocked_domains
    )


def normalize_email(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    collector: ValidationCollector,
) -> NormalizedEmail | None:
    raw = required_string(payload, "email", collector)
    if raw is None:
        return None

    if len(raw) > MAX_EMAIL_RAW_CHARS:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "too_long",
            "Email address is too long.",
        )
        return None

    if has_forbidden_unicode(raw):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_unicode",
            "Email contains prohibited control or invisible characters.",
        )
        return None

    raw_bytes = utf8_size(raw)
    if raw_bytes is None:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_unicode",
            "Email contains invalid Unicode.",
        )
        return None

    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", raw.strip())

    if not normalized:
        collector.add("email", "empty", "Email cannot be empty.")
        return None

    if any(character.isspace() for character in normalized):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "whitespace",
            "Email cannot contain whitespace.",
        )

    if normalized.count("@") != 1:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_format",
            "Email must be a valid address.",
        )
        return None

    supplied_domain = normalized.rsplit("@", 1)[1]
    if supplied_domain.endswith("."):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "trailing_dot",
            "Email domain cannot end with a dot.",
        )

    try:
        result = validate_email(
            normalized,
            check_deliverability=False,
            allow_smtputf8=False,
        )
    except EmailNotValidError:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_format",
            "Email must be a valid address.",
        )
        return None

    local = result.local_part
    unicode_domain = result.domain

    if not local.isascii() or not EMAIL_LOCAL_RE.fullmatch(local):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "unsupported_local_part",
            "Email local part must use standard ASCII dot-atom syntax.",
        )

    if (
        local.startswith(".")
        or local.endswith(".")
        or ".." in local
        or len(local.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")) > 64
    ):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_local_part",
            "Email local part is invalid.",
        )

    try:
        ascii_domain = (
            result.ascii_domain
            or idna.encode(
                unicode_domain,
                uts46=True,
                std3_rules=True,
            ).decode("ascii")
        ).casefold()
        decoded_domain = idna.decode(
            ascii_domain.encode("ascii"),
            uts46=True,
            std3_rules=True,
        )
    except idna.IDNAError:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_idn",
            "Email domain is not a valid internationalized domain.",
        )
        return None

    if len(ascii_domain) > 253 or "." not in ascii_domain:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_domain",
            "Email must use a fully qualified public domain.",
        )

    try:
        ipaddress.ip_address(ascii_domain.strip("[]"))
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "domain_literal",
            "IP-address email domains are not accepted.",
        )

    labels = ascii_domain.split(".")
    if any(
        not label
        or len(label) > 63
        or label.startswith("-")
        or label.endswith("-")
        for label in labels
    ):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_domain",
            "Email domain has an invalid label.",
        )

    tld = labels[-1] if labels else ""
    if (
        len(tld) < 2
        or tld.isdigit()
        or (
            not tld.startswith("xn--")
            and not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]{2,63}", tld)
        )
    ):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "invalid_tld",
            "Email domain has an invalid top-level domain.",
        )

    for label in decoded_domain.split("."):
        if label_has_mixed_scripts(label):
            collector.add(
                "email",
                "mixed_script_domain",
                "Email domain contains a suspicious mixture of writing systems.",
            )
            break

    if (
        ascii_domain in SPECIAL_USE_DOMAINS
        or ascii_domain.endswith(SPECIAL_USE_SUFFIXES)
    ):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "non_public_domain",
            "Email must use a public mail domain.",
        )

    if domain_matches(ascii_domain, DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS):
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "disposable_domain",
            "Disposable email addresses are not accepted.",
        )

    if BLOCK_ROLE_EMAILS and local.casefold() in ROLE_EMAIL_LOCALS:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "role_address",
            "Shared or role-based email addresses are not accepted.",
        )

    canonical = f"{local.casefold()}@{ascii_domain}"
    if len(canonical.encode("utf-8")) > MAX_EMAIL_BYTES:
        collector.add(
            "email",
            "too_long",
            "Email address exceeds the maximum encoded length.",
        )

    return NormalizedEmail(
        canonical=canonical,
        local=local.casefold(),
        domain=ascii_domain,
    )


def normalize_username(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    collector: ValidationCollector,
) -> NormalizedUsername | None:
    raw = required_string(payload, "username", collector)
    if raw is None:
        return None

    if len(raw) > MAX_USERNAME_RAW_CHARS:
        collector.add("username", "too_long", "Username is too long.")
        return None

    if has_forbidden_unicode(raw):
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "invalid_unicode",
            "Username contains prohibited control or invisible characters.",
        )
        return None

    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", raw.strip())

    if not normalized:
        collector.add("username", "empty", "Username cannot be empty.")
        return None

    if not MIN_USERNAME_CHARS <= len(normalized) <= MAX_USERNAME_CHARS:
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "length",
            f"Username must contain {MIN_USERNAME_CHARS} to "
            f"{MAX_USERNAME_CHARS} characters.",
        )

    # Usernames are security identifiers, so the policy deliberately restricts
    # them to ASCII. NFKC still safely converts full-width ASCII before checks.
    if not normalized.isascii():
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "non_ascii",
            "Username may contain ASCII letters, numbers, dot, underscore, and hyphen only.",
        )
        return None

    if not USERNAME_RE.fullmatch(normalized):
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "invalid_characters",
            "Username must start with a letter and contain only letters, numbers, dot, underscore, or hyphen.",
        )

    if normalized.endswith((".", "_", "-")):
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "trailing_separator",
            "Username cannot end with a separator.",
        )

    if re.search(r"[._-]{2}", normalized):
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "repeated_separator",
            "Username cannot contain adjacent separators.",
        )

    key = normalized.casefold()
    skeleton = identifier_skeleton(key)

    protected = (
        skeleton in RESERVED_USERNAMES
        or any(
            skeleton.startswith(reserved)
            and skeleton[len(reserved):].isdigit()
            for reserved in RESERVED_USERNAMES
        )
        or any(
            bounded_edit_distance(skeleton, reserved) <= 1
            for reserved in CRITICAL_RESERVED_USERNAMES
        )
    )
    if protected:
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "reserved",
            "That username is reserved.",
        )

    profanity_candidate = re.sub(r"[._-]+", " ", key)
    if profanity.contains_profanity(profanity_candidate):
        collector.add(
            "username",
            "offensive",
            "Username violates the content policy.",
        )

    return NormalizedUsername(
        display=normalized,
        key=key,
        skeleton=skeleton,
    )


def normalize_display_name(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    collector: ValidationCollector,
) -> str | None:
    raw = required_string(payload, "display_name", collector)
    if raw is None:
        return None

    if len(raw) > MAX_DISPLAY_RAW_CHARS:
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "too_long",
            "Display name is too long.",
        )
        return None

    if has_forbidden_unicode(raw):
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "invalid_unicode",
            "Display name contains prohibited control or invisible characters.",
        )
        return None

    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", raw)
    normalized = regex.sub(r"\p{White_Space}+", " ", normalized).strip()

    if not normalized:
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "empty",
            "Display name cannot be empty.",
        )
        return None

    grapheme_count = len(regex.findall(r"\X", normalized))
    if grapheme_count > MAX_DISPLAY_GRAPHEMES:
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "too_long",
            f"Display name may contain at most {MAX_DISPLAY_GRAPHEMES} characters.",
        )

    encoded_size = utf8_size(normalized)
    if encoded_size is None or encoded_size > 240:
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "encoded_length",
            "Display name exceeds the maximum encoded length.",
        )

    # Store canonical plain text, not pre-escaped HTML. Pre-escaping at storage
    # causes double-encoding bugs; every HTML consumer must still use textContent
    # or contextual output escaping.
    if "<" in normalized or ">" in normalized:
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "markup",
            "Display name cannot contain HTML markup.",
        )

    if HTML_ENTITY_RE.search(normalized) or SCRIPT_SCHEME_RE.search(normalized):
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "unsafe_content",
            "Display name contains unsafe content.",
        )

    if profanity.contains_profanity(normalized):
        collector.add(
            "display_name",
            "offensive",
            "Display name violates the content policy.",
        )

    return normalized


def normalize_password(
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    collector: ValidationCollector,
    *,
    email: NormalizedEmail | None,
    username: NormalizedUsername | None,
    display_name: str | None,
) -> str | None:
    raw = required_string(payload, "password", collector)
    if raw is None:
        return None

    # Enforce limits before Argon2, zxcvbn, regexes, or breach lookups.
    if len(raw) > MAX_PASSWORD_CHARS:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "too_long",
            f"Password may contain at most {MAX_PASSWORD_CHARS} characters.",
        )
        return None

    if has_forbidden_unicode(raw):
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "invalid_unicode",
            "Password contains prohibited control or invisible characters.",
        )
        return None

    raw_size = utf8_size(raw)
    if raw_size is None or raw_size > MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "encoded_length",
            f"Password may contain at most {MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES} encoded bytes.",
        )
        return None

    # Authentication must apply this same NFC normalization before verification.
    password = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw)

    if len(password) < MIN_PASSWORD_CHARS:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "too_short",
            f"Password must contain at least {MIN_PASSWORD_CHARS} characters.",
        )

    if password and (password[0].isspace() or password[-1].isspace()):
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "outer_whitespace",
            "Password cannot begin or end with whitespace.",
        )

    if any(character.isspace() and character != " " for character in password):
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "ambiguous_whitespace",
            "Password may use ordinary spaces but not other whitespace characters.",
        )

    character_classes = sum(
        (
            any(character.islower() for character in password),
            any(character.isupper() for character in password),
            any(character.isdigit() for character in password),
            any(
                unicodedata.category(character)[0] in {"P", "S"}
                for character in password
            ),
        )
    )
    if character_classes < 3:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "character_classes",
            "Password must use at least three of: lowercase, uppercase, number, and symbol.",
        )

    if len(set(password.casefold())) < 6:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "low_variety",
            "Password contains too little character variety.",
        )

    if re.search(r"(.)\1{3,}", password, flags=re.DOTALL):
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "repeated_characters",
            "Password contains an excessive repeated-character pattern.",
        )

    compact = identifier_skeleton(password)
    if compact in COMMON_PASSWORDS:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "common",
            "Password is too common.",
        )

    sequences = (
        "0123456789",
        "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz",
        "qwertyuiop",
        "asdfghjkl",
        "zxcvbnm",
    )
    compact_casefold = password.casefold()
    sequence_found = False
    for sequence in sequences:
        for index in range(len(sequence) - 3):
            fragment = sequence[index:index + 4]
            if (
                fragment in compact_casefold
                or fragment[::-1] in compact_casefold
            ):
                sequence_found = True
                break
        if sequence_found:
            break

    if sequence_found:
        collector.add(
            "password",
            "sequence",
            "Password contains an easily guessed sequence.",
        )

    identifiers: list[str] = []
    if username:
        identifiers.extend((username.key, username.skeleton))
    if email:
        identifiers.extend(
            (
                email.local,
                email.domain,
                email.domain.split(".", 1)[0],
            )
        )
    if display_name:
        identifiers.extend(
            token.casefold()
            for token in regex.findall(r"[\p{L}\p{N}]+", display_name)
            if len(token) >= 3
        )

    password_identifier = identifier_skeleton(password)
    for identifier in identifiers:
        candidate = identifier_skeleton(identifier)
        if len(candidate) < 3:
            continue

        if candidate in password_identifier:
            collector.add(
                "password",

@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def domain_accepts_email(domain: str) -> bool:
    resolver = dns.resolver.Resolver(configure=True)
    resolver.timeout = 1.25
    resolver.lifetime = 2.5
    query_name = f"{domain}."

    try:
        answer = resolver.resolve(query_name, "MX", search=False)
        exchanges = [
            record.exchange.to_text().rstrip(".")
            for record in answer
        ]
        # RFC 7505 null MX: "MX 0 ."
        return any(exchanges)
    except (dns.resolver.NXDOMAIN, dns.resolver.YXDOMAIN):
        return False
    except dns.resolver.NoAnswer:
        pass
    except (
        dns.resolver.NoNameservers,
        dns.resolver.LifetimeTimeout,
        dns.exception.Timeout,
    ) as exc:
        raise DependencyUnavailable("DNS lookup unavailable") from exc

    # RFC mail delivery may fall back to A/AAAA when MX is absent.
    for record_type in ("A", "AAAA"):
        try:
            answer = resolver.resolve(
                query_name,
                record_type,
                search=False,
            )
            if answer:
                return True
        except (dns.resolver.NXDOMAIN, dns.resolver.YXDOMAIN):
            return False
        except dns.resolver.NoAnswer:
            continue
        except (
            dns.resolver.NoNameservers,
            dns.resolver.LifetimeTimeout,
            dns.exception.Timeout,
        ) as exc:
            raise DependencyUnavailable("DNS lookup unavailable") from exc

    return False


def pwned_password_count(password: str) -> int:
    # HIBP's k-anonymity protocol mandates SHA-1 for deriving the range prefix.
    # The digest is never stored and is never used as a password verifier.
    digest = hashlib.sha1(
        password.encode("utf-8"),
        usedforsecurity=False,
    ).hexdigest().upper()
    prefix, suffix = digest[:5], digest[5:]

    try:
        with httpx.Client(
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(3.0, connect=1.5),
            follow_redirects=False,
            verify=True,
        ) as client:
            response = client.get(
                f"https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/{prefix}",
                headers={
                    "Add-Padding": "true",
                    "Accept": "text/plain",
                    "Accept-Encoding": "identity",
                    "User-Agent": "secure-registration-service/1.0",
                },
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise DependencyUnavailable(
            "Breached-password service unavailable"
        ) from exc

    if len(response.content) > 2_000_000:
        raise DependencyUnavailable(
            "Breached-password response exceeded safety limit"
        )

    for line in response.text.splitlines():
        returned_suffix, separator, count_text = line.partition(":")
        if (
            separator
            and len(returned_suffix) == 35
            and hmac.compare_digest(returned_suffix.upper(), suffix)
        ):
            try:
                return int(count_text.strip())
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise DependencyUnavailable(
                    "Invalid breached-password response"
                ) from exc

    return 0

def canonical_origin(value: str, *, allow_path: bool = False) -> str | None:
    try:
        parsed = urlsplit(value)
        port = parsed.port
    except ValueError:
        return None

    if (
        parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https"}
        or not parsed.hostname
        or parsed.username is not None
        or parsed.password is not None
        or parsed.query
        or parsed.fragment
        or (not allow_path and parsed.path not in {"", "/"})
    ):
        return None

    host = parsed.hostname.casefold()
    try:
        address = ipaddress.ip_address(host)
        host = address.compressed
        if address.version == 6:
            host = f"[{host}]"
    except ValueError:
        try:
            host = idna.encode(
                host,
                uts46=True,
                std3_rules=True,
            ).decode("ascii").casefold()
        except idna.IDNAError:
            return None

    default_port = (
        parsed.scheme == "http" and port in {None, 80}
    ) or (
        parsed.scheme == "https" and port in {None, 443}
    )
    port_component = "" if default_port else f":{port}"

    return f"{parsed.scheme}://{host}{port_component}"

def enforce_same_origin(request: Request) -> None:
    origin_header = request.headers.get("origin")
    fetch_site = request.headers.get("sec-fetch-site", "").casefold()

    if origin_header:
        origin = canonical_origin(origin_header)
        if origin is None or origin not in ALLOWED_ORIGINS:
            raise APIProblem(
                403,
                "cross_origin_request",

            403,

        referer = request.headers.get("referer")
        referer_origin = (

def normalized_peer_address(request: Request) -> str:
    # Do not trust X-Forwarded-For here. Configure Uvicorn's trusted proxy list
    # so request.client is rewritten only by a known reverse proxy.
    peer = request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"

    try:
        address = ipaddress.ip_address(peer.split("%", 1)[0])
    except ValueError:
        return "unknown"

    if address.version == 6:
        network = ipaddress.ip_network(f"{address}/64", strict=False)
        return f"{network.network_address.compressed}/64"

    return address.compressed

def reject_duplicate_keys(
    pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]],

def reject_json_constant(_: str) -> None:

async def read_json_object(request: Request) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if request.url.query:
        raise APIProblem(
            400,
            "unexpected_query",
            "Query parameters are not accepted by this endpoint.",
        )

    content_encoding = request.headers.get(
        "content-encoding", "identity"
    ).casefold()
    if content_encoding != "identity":
        raise APIProblem(
            415,
            "unsupported_content_encoding",
            "Compressed request bodies are not accepted.",
        )

    content_type_parts = [
        part.strip()
        for part in request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";")
    ]
    if not content_type_parts or content_type_parts[0].casefold() != "application/json":
        raise APIProblem(
            415,
            "unsupported_media_type",
            "Content-Type must be application/json.",
        )

    for parameter in content_type_parts[1:]:
        name, separator, value = parameter.partition("=")
        if (
            not separator
            or name.strip().casefold() != "charset"
            or value.strip().strip('"').casefold() not in {"utf-8", "utf8"}
        ):
            raise APIProblem(
                415,
                "unsupported_media_type_parameter",
                "Only UTF-8 JSON is accepted.",
            )

    content_length = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if content_length is not None:
        try:
            declared_length = int(content_length)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise APIProblem(
                400,
                "invalid_content_length",
                "Invalid Content-Length header.",
            ) from exc

        if declared_length < 0:
            raise APIProblem(
                400,
                "invalid_content_length",
                "Invalid Content-Length header.",
            )
        if declared_length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise APIProblem(
                413,
                "body_too_large",
                "Request body is too large.",
            )

    body = bytearray()
    async for chunk in request.stream():
        if len(body) + len(chunk) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise APIProblem(
                413,
                "body_too_large",
                "Request body is too large.",
            )
        body.extend(chunk)

    if not body:
        raise APIProblem(
            400,
            "empty_body",
            "A JSON request body is required.",
        )

    try:
        decoded = bytes(body).decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
        payload = json.loads(
            decoded,
            object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicate_keys,
            parse_constant=reject_json_constant,
        )
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise APIProblem(
            400,
            "invalid_encoding",
            "Request body must be valid UTF-8.",
        ) from exc
    except DuplicateJSONKey as exc:
        raise APIProblem(
            400,
            "duplicate_json_key",
            "Duplicate JSON object keys are not accepted.",
        ) from exc
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError) as exc:
        raise APIProblem(
            400,
            "malformed_json",
            "Request body must be valid JSON.",
        ) from exc

    if type(payload) is not dict:
        raise APIProblem(
            400,
            "invalid_body",
            "Request body must be a JSON object.",
        )

    return payload

    if CHECK_PWNED_PASSWORDS and password is not None:

                run_in_threadpool(

            *(awaitable for _, awaitable in checks),
            return_exceptions=True,

            503,
            "storage_unavailable",
            "Registration is temporarily unavailable.",
